title: Oscar Predictions: Animated Feature — A New and Competitive Era for the Medium That Isn’t Just for Kids
description:
Nov 3, 2026 12:25pm PT	
	

	
	Oscar Predictions: Animated Feature — A New and Competitive Era for the Medium That Isn’t Just for Kids
body:
Nov 3, 2026 12:25pm PT	
	

	
	Oscar Predictions: Animated Feature — A New and Competitive Era for the Medium That Isn’t Just for Kids
	
										

				


					

									IFC
	

					
		
	Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.
	



	

					“Wildwood“
									Courtesy of Laika
	




	Best Animated Feature Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 3, 2026): This year, animated features aren’t just for kids. And that’s a good thing.

	Laika’s “Wildwood” is the company’s first PG-13 film in its 17 years as a feature studio. At 130 minutes, it ties the record for the longest English-language animated film ever made. Director and producer Travis Knight is already an Oscar nominee for “Kubo and the Two Strings” and has earned considerable respect from his peers and audiences alike. “Wildwood” is among the year’s most acclaimed films and, despite a less-than-stellar box office performance, currently looks like the one to beat.

	Knight was among the filmmakers featured in this year’s Pixels and Pencils panel, Variety’s conversation with animation directors at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival. He was joined by Brad Bird (“Ray Gunn”), Daniel Chong (“Hoppers”), Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado (“Forgotten Island”) and Leah Nelson (“Tangles”), all of whom are also in the animated feature race.

	And that’s just the group represented on the panel. Louis Clichy’s “Iron Boy” and Andrew Stanton’s “Toy Story 5” are among the other contenders helping make this one of the category’s most competitive lineups in recent years.

	Since “Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio” won the animated feature Oscar at the 95th Academy Awards, neither Disney nor Pixar has won the trophy. Instead, “The Boy and the Heron,” “Flow” and “KPop Demon Hunters” have taken home the prize, marking a significant shift for a category largely dominated by those two studios since “Shrek” won the inaugural award in 2002.

	Then there’s “Tangles,” a film that makes no attempt to disguise its ambitions as an adult story. First-time feature director Leah Nelson co-wrote the film with Sarah Leavitt, adapting Leavitt’s graphic memoir about her mother’s battle with Alzheimer’s disease in the late 1990s. Abbi Jacobson voices Sarah, while Julia Louis-Dreyfus plays her mother. Louis-Dreyfus is also a producer, alongside Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen.
	

	Both “Tangles” and “Wildwood” are also being submitted in the drama categories at the Golden Globes, where animated films have traditionally defaulted to comedy. It’s technically a matter of category placement, but it also signals something about how these creative teams want their films to be perceived.Of course, none of this is entirely new. “Persepolis” and “Anomalisa” earned Oscar nominations years ago, and Japanese filmmakers have been making animation for adults for as long as the medium has existed.

	Only three animated films — “Beauty and the Beast,” “Up” and “Toy Story 3″ — have ever earned best picture nominations, and the last of those came 15 years ago. In a year where we could find our first documentary feature nominated for best picture (“You Can See Everything”), could an animated film join the lineup, too?

	The list of predictions in all categories can be found here.

	The Governors Awards, which will hand out honorary Oscars to Glenn Close and Ridley Scott, will take place Sunday, Nov. 15. Preliminary voting for the Oscars shortlist in 12 categories runs Dec. 7-11, with the shortlist announcement to follow Tuesday, Dec. 15. Following the close of the eligibility period on Dec. 31, 2026, nominations voting will run Jan. 11-15, 2027. The official Oscar nominations will be announced on Thursday, Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Oscars will take place on Sunday, March 14, 2027 and will be hosted by Conan O’Brien. The ceremony airs live at 7 p.m. ET on ABC and in more than 200 territories worldwide from the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood.



	

									“Iron Boy” / Sony Pictures Classics

title: ‘Cher Adores Michael Douglas,’ Icon’s Rep Says After Douglas Disses Her Oscar Win for ‘Moonstruck’
description: Cher is responding with grace to Michael Douglas‘ viral diss over her 1988 Oscar win for “Moonstruck.” A representative for the music and acting ic
body:
Cher is responding with grace to Michael Douglas‘ viral diss over her 1988 Oscar win for “Moonstruck.” A representative for the music and acting icon told Entertainment Weekly point blank: “Cher adores Michael Douglas.”

	At the 60th Academy Awards in April 1988, Cher took home the prize for best actress over Douglas’ “Fatal Attraction” co-star Glenn Close. Douglas still disagrees with the Academy’s decision nearly 40 years later. Appearing alongside Close on a recent episode of “The Graham Norton Show,” Douglas noted that “she should have won [the Oscar] with ‘Fatal Attraction'” and that Close “was nominated, I believe, [for] her fourth” Oscar by that time. When the actor noted Cher won the Oscar instead, Norton responded, “Oh wow,” prompting Douglas to diss Cher: “I know, that’s what we all said!”
	

	“Michael, be kind,” Close then responded while turning to Douglas as the studio audience laughed. 

	All three actors attended the 1988 Oscars as nominees, with Cher winning best actress for “Moonstruck” and Douglas winning best actor for his role in Oliver Stone’s “Wall Street.” Douglas was the sole nominee for his movie, while “Moonstruck” was up for six awards, including best picture. The romantic comedy also won Oscars for adapted screenplay and supporting actress (Olympia Dukakis). “Fatal Attraction,” meanwhile, was also nominated for six Oscars but went home empty handed. Both movies battled for best picture and best director but lost to “The Last Emperor” and Bernardo Bertolucci, respectively. 

	As noted by Douglas, Close went into the 1988 Oscars as a four-time Oscar nominee. She had previously earned three nominations in the best supporting actress category for “The World According to Garp,” “The Big Chill” and “The Natural.” “Fatal Attraction” marked Close’s first best actress nomination. She would go on to be nominated at the Oscars four more times for “Dangerous Liaisons,” “Albert Nobbs,” “The Wife” and “Hillbilly Elegy.” She has yet to win a competitive Oscar but will be awarded an honorary statue at the Governors Awards this month.
	

	Cher, meanwhile, won the Oscar for “Moonstruck” after previously picking up a nomination for best supporting actress in 1984 for “Silkwood.”

schema.headline: ‘Cher Adores Michael Douglas,’ Icon’s Rep Says After Douglas Disses Her Oscar Win for ‘Moonstruck’

title: James Wan and Jason Blum Unveil New Company Name: Blumhouse Atomic
description: James Wan and Jason Blum have unveiled a new umbrella title for their merged horror production companies, Blumhouse and Atomic Monster: Blumhouse A
body:
James Wan and Jason Blum have unveiled a new umbrella title for their merged horror production companies, Blumhouse and Atomic Monster: Blumhouse Atomic. Blumhouse and Atomic Monster will continue to operate as distinct production labels, and their respective creative teams will develop and produce film and television projects under each banner.

	“When we merged our companies, we believed the whole would be greater than the sum of its parts and that is exactly what has happened,” said Jason Blum, Co-Founder of Blumhouse Atomic. “Blumhouse Atomic is a natural evolution of what we’ve built together. ‘The Conjuring’ franchise, ‘Insidious,’ ‘Saw,’ no filmmaker has created more horror franchises than James Wan, and together we’ve brought some of the genre’s most recognizable properties under one roof. Bringing ‘Saw’ back to James, with a new chapter on the way, is a perfect example of what we can do together. We have the output of a studio with the creative freedom and financial discipline of an independent company, and more opportunities than ever to take these stories beyond the theater and into television, games and live experiences.”
	

	Wan and Blum merged Blumhouse and Atomic Monster in 2024, bringing together two of the most productive and successful production houses and execs in the horror space. The combined banners have since generated more than $2.5 billion in worldwide box office against combined production budgets of less than $330 million. In 2026, Blumhouse Atomic pulled in $1.3 billion, riding the wave of two of the year’s biggest hits in Curry Barker’s “Obsession” ($520 million worldwide) and Kane Parsons’ “Backrooms” ($400 million worldwide).
	

	“The future of horror comes from new voices, and Blumhouse Atomic gives us more ways to find them and support them for the long haul,” added James Wan, Co-Founder of Blumhouse Atomic. “I got my start with a small film and people willing to take a chance on it, so creating those opportunities for others is personal to me. Working with filmmakers like Kane Parsons, Curry Barker, Josh Giuliano and Dylan Clark is a big part of that. We want to give them the freedom to make something distinctive and build relationships that last beyond one film.”

	Blumhouse Atomic’s mission of cultivating blockbuster horror hits from undersized budgets was further bolstered this year with the appointment of Sam Zimmerman as senior vice president of development and acquisitions, who was tasked with developing a slate of genre features with budgets of under $5 million. The company also recently inked a first-look deal with Divide/Conquer to develop high-concept projects for an economical rate. 

	Blumhouse Atomic’s 2027 film slate includes “River,” “The Revenge of La Llorona,” “The Exorcist: Martyrs,” “Anything But Ghosts,” “Paranormal Activity,” “Molepeople,” “Blair Witch,” “Sleepover” and “Seasons.”

schema.headline: James Wan and Jason Blum Unveil New Company Name: Blumhouse Atomic

title: ‘The Elder Scrolls 6’ Title Revealed (Gaming News Roundup)
description:
Bethesda Game Studios has officially revealed the subtitle and logo for “The Elder Scrolls 6.”

	The sixth edition was announced as “Sentinel” alon
body:
Bethesda Game Studios has officially revealed the subtitle and logo for “The Elder Scrolls 6.”

	The sixth edition was announced as “Sentinel” alongside a logo reveal in a video message from longtime franchise director Todd Howard as part of Bethesda’s 40th anniversary Tuesday. The game will serve as the followup to “Skyrim,” the 2011 installation in the role-playing franchise.


	Sentinel is a city within the Hammerfell province on Tamriel, the continent where “The Elder Scrolls” is set. Hammerfell is west of Cyrodiil, where the fourth installment “Oblivion” (2006) took place, and southwest of “Skyrim,” which is still the studio’s most played game.
	

	“The Elder Scrolls 6” was first announced in 2018 during Bethesda’s E3 2018 conference and entered active production in 2023 after the launch of “Starfield.” Howard said in 2021 that he anticipated the game could be released 15-17 years after “Skyrim,” potentially putting fans still a few years away from playing “Sentinel.”

	See more gaming news from the week in the roundup below.
	
		UPCOMING GAMES	

	As the release of “Grand Theft Auto VI” looms closer, digital pre-loading is set to begin on Nov. 10.

	Players can pre-load the game on PlayStation 5 at midnight local time in respective time zones and on XBOX Series X and S at midnight GMT. The pre-load file will require up to 212 GB depending on the device, and code-in-box versions for both consoles is set to be available from retailers starting Nov. 12. Details on how to pre-load “GTA 6” are available on the Rockstar Support website.
	

	Rockstar Games will also add a printable “GTA 6” cover art poster and map of Leonida as a free digital download to the website on Nov. 29. A double-sided physical version will later be available shortly after launch.
	
		RELEASE DATES	

	“Petit Planet,” a cozy galactic life simulation game from HoYoverse, will launch on Dec. 4.

	Players enter the game as Planet Tenders on a journey to the Starsea on the back of a spirit that listens to the wishes in people’s hearts. Neighbors visit the planet to share stories, and players can explore the Islets across the Starsea or visit the Galactic Bazaar for games and auctions.

	HoYoverse has a series of events and rewards tied to the upcoming game launch, including a pre-registration drawing for prizes, a team event for an exclusive clothing item and more.

	The game will be available for cross-platform play on PC, iOS and Android, with Nintendo Switch 2 launch in 2027.

	Watch the launch trailer below.


	
		DATA/SALES	

	The “Borderlands” franchise has crossed 100 million units sold.

	“Borderlands 4” released in September 2025, and Gearbox’s development team is working on additional content. Over the past year, two story packs, five bounty packs, two vault hunters, two free raid boss encounters, “Takedown” endgame raid and more have been added.

	Starting Nov. 6, players will participate in The Hunt. Earlier this year, the community fundraising event raised $118,995.80 for St. Jude’s Children Research Hospital. 2K Foundations and Gearbox will match every dollar donated up to the previous record amount.

	Titles across the franchise are now on sale, and “Borderlands 4” is available for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC through Steam and the Epic Games Store.

schema.headline: ‘The Elder Scrolls 6’ Title Revealed (Gaming News Roundup)

title: Netflix Orders YA Drama ‘Prep’ Based on Curtis Sittenfeld Novel From Nicole Taylor
description:
Netflix has given a straight-to-series order to the drama “Prep,” based on the novel of the same name by Curtis Sittenfeld. 

	The show is official
body:
Netflix has given a straight-to-series order to the drama “Prep,” based on the novel of the same name by Curtis Sittenfeld. 

	The show is officially described as a coming-of-age story about “scholarship girl Lee Fiora’s high school years at Ault, a prestigious New England boarding school, and her journey to navigate friendship, crushes and class as a fish out of water among her privileged, confident classmates.”


	Nicole Taylor will adapt the book for the screen and will serve as showrunner and executive producer. Will Ferrell, Jessica Elbaum, and Alix Taylor will executive produce for Gloria Sanchez Productions. Sittenfeld is also an executive producer. 
	

	“’Prep’ is my all time favourite novel and I have longed to adapt it for the entire twenty years since I first read it and found myself reflected uncannily back,” Taylor said. “There is no more acute depiction of the introspective, bookish self-conscious adolescent girl and no more truthful or excoriating take on the perils of social mobility than in Curtis Sittenfeld’s beautiful first novel. I am overjoyed to be adapting for Netflix.” 

	Taylor most recently created the popular series “One Day” starring Leo Woodall and Ambika Mod, which aired on Netflix in 2024. Her other credits include the feature “The Wild Rose” and shows like “Three Girls,” “Dracula,” and “The White Queen.” 

	She is repped by Curtis Brown Group and UTA. 

	“I’m overjoyed that Netflix is making ‘Prep’ as a TV show–the 22-year wait was worth it! Alix Taylor at Gloria Sanchez has guided the project forward with such intelligence and enthusiasm, and Nicole Taylor’s scripts are truly brilliant,” Sittenfeld added. “Nicole’s adaptation makes me understand my own novel, and myself, better. My 51-year-old self can’t wait to see what they do with this story of privilege, longing, and teen angst.”
	

	Gloria Sanchez has a long history with Netflix, most recently producing Ferrell’s golf comedy series “The Hawk.” The company has also produced shows like “Dead to Me,” “No Good Deed,” and “The Woman in the House Across the Street from the Girl in the Window.”

schema.headline: Netflix Orders YA Drama ‘Prep’ Based on Curtis Sittenfeld Novel From Nicole Taylor

title: Netflix Launches First AI-Branded Content Recommendations Feature on TVs
description: Netflix, which has seen viewer engagement slide in recent quarters, is turning to AI for a new feature aimed at spurring users to find something ne
body:
Netflix, which has seen viewer engagement slide in recent quarters, is turning to AI for a new feature aimed at spurring users to find something new to watch.

	The company on Tuesday (Nov. 3) is debuting AI Discover, a new feature on the Netflix TV app, initially to a limited number of subscribers in the U.S. In the first iteration of the new AI-based tool, you are prompted to explore content based on preset themes (such as “Something Light,” “Scare Me,” “Workplace Comedy Favorites,” “Family Movie Night,” “Quick Watches,” “Family Scandal Sagas” or “Royal Court Intrigue”). The recommended titles are produced in real time, according to Netflix, based on a user’s viewing history and preferences as well as what’s trending on the platform.
	

	The streamer will begin rolling out AI Discover in the U.S. to customers who use Netflix in English on supported smart TVs. If you have access to it, you will see a “Discover” tab with a red gem-shaped icon and a “New” label in the top navigation bar on your TV. The company plans to expand the feature to more regions and customers in the coming weeks.

	Netflix has long used machine-learning and AI technologies to personalize content recommendations, but AI Discover is the first user-facing application that the company is branding as powered by artificial intelligence. The hope is that the AI-recommended titles will be another tool to drive up Netflix’s total watch time among viewers, especially in the U.S. Amid a recent drop-off in per-subscriber viewing, Netflix overhauled its content leadership team, which included replacing content chief Bela Bajaria with industry veteran Peter Rice in a bid to produce more hits.
	

	The AI content recommendation feature is interactive, but it’s not a chatbot-like experience. AI Discover will not be available on kids’ profiles.

	When you click on the Discover button on the Netflix interface, it shows a message that says, “Give me a moment while I find your next obsession.” Here’s how the theme-based AI Discover experience works, according to Netflix:


Pick from a range of themes, each previewed with a clip from a show or movie. Some match a mood (“Something Light,” “Scare Me”), an intended audience (“Family Movie Night”) or how much time you have (“Quick Watches”). Others might reflect what’s new or popular, or what you’ve been watching lately.
The app displays an array of matching movie or TV show recommendations.
You can then pick from more specific themes to continue searching; or you can select “Something Different” for a fresh set.
Every title has a “Tune Your Recommendations” button, right next to “Play” and “My List.” Use it to keep a recommendation, or to ask Netflix to not recommend something again.



	Netflix is positioning the AI-powered recommendation feature as a work in progress — and it says it wants customers to provide input about how useful they find it. “Think of AI Discover as our test kitchen: we’re trying out new recipes for discovery, and your use and feedback help us decide which ones to keep, improve or serve up next,” Netflix says in a blog post about the new feature. “Some may even make their way into the main Netflix experience.”

	AI Discover is powered by a “new intelligence layer we’ve been building that responds to what members tell us in real time and keeps learning,” according to Netflix.

	“What we’re most excited about is how it feels to use,” the company says. “Tell us what you’re after, and the experience adjusts. Tell us a recommendation isn’t for you, and we’ll remember it in AI Discover, so it won’t keep turning up.”

	Netflix has also adopted AI in other areas of its business. About 300 titles across the streamer’s library have used generative AI across their production process, the company announced in July. This spring, Netflix paid $587 million to buy Ben Affleck-founded company InterPositive, which it says gives filmmakers AI tools to use throughout film and TV productions.

	— Corbin Bolies contributed to this article

schema.headline: Netflix Launches First AI-Branded Content Recommendations Feature on TVs

title: What Election Day Commentators Are Saying: Trump Rants, Hasan Piker Wonders if MAGA ‘Cult’ Is Over and More (Updating)
description: It’s Election Day in America, which means that pundits were falling over each other to discuss the day’s results as soon as the polls opened. At st
body:
It’s Election Day in America, which means that pundits were falling over each other to discuss the day’s results as soon as the polls opened. At stake: all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and plenty of high-profile state races. Here’s what some of the country’s loudest and most influential talkers had to say about America’s big vote day.
	
		Donald Trump	

	Trump started his Election Day rants early, taking to Truth Social to say, “Abdul El-Sayed Hates Jews and Hates Blacks. Don’t feel bad, he also Hates Whites. Only fools would vote for him in the Michigan race for the U.S. Senate! He will, 100%, do you in!”
	

	He called into “Fox & Friends” later in the morning to go on a lengthy diatribe about everything on his mind, including why the war in Iran isn’t a big deal.

	“Iran had threat of a nuclear weapon,” Trump said. “Iran is No. 1 state sponsor of terror in the world. They are the meanest. They are very tough. I see why Middle East was afraid of them. They’re very tough, but they have been decapitated. They have no Navy. They had 159 ships.

	“Every ship is at the bottom of the sea, every airplane is laying in small pieces, tiny pieces all over the runway. No anti-aircraft, we took some out last night,” he continued. “Minor attack, wasn’t war. They built an anti-aircraft facility, it took them about two months. We watched it get built. We hit it last night nicely, not big war. You talk about war, this is not really war. We have — hit them hard at the beginning, but that was it. We knocked out their nuclear capability and dust, thousands of tons of rocks, we have that under surveillance, if anyone went there we’d hit it again. We have Space Force I developed my first term. We can see the badge, name tag on man’s chest from outer space. It’s the most unbelievable stuff you’ve ever seen.”
	


	
		Hasan Piker	

	The outspoken Twitch streamer took to X early in the day to muse about some big questions, writing, “we’re abt to find out how much ‘cult’ still remains in maga today. Is it over? Is it still strong? how well does racial polarization & pure vitriol work on Americans after experiencing negative real wage growth? can trump truly reverse every single campaign promise & still maintain the cattle vote?”
	
		Pod Save America	

	On the Election Day morning edition of the podcast, the trio of hosts were bullish on a blue wave. When Jon Favreau asked if not winning both chambers will feel like a loss for Democrats at this point, Jon Lovett gave a passionate response.

	“In this environment, with a President this despicable, with an illegal war, with the tariffs, with a Republican Congress rubber-stamping this ridiculous, vile, lawless administration, if we can’t win both chambers, then yes, that will be a loss,” Lovett said.


	
		Morning Joe	

	On MS Now, Joe Scarborough called the Republican Party’s closing arguments “astronomically stupid.”

	“You have Ramaswamy talking about Communism, right?” Scarborough said. “And there is no Communism here. Amy Acton has no Communist views, Donald Trump does … It’s not what the Democrats are doing, but they’re talking about Communism instead of talking about the price of the cost of gas, Communism instead of the cost of diesel, Communism instead of the cost of groceries. I’m not good at this political stuff, but I think that and a reflecting pool doesn’t add up to victory for Republicans today.”

schema.headline: What Election Day Commentators Are Saying: Trump Rants, Hasan Piker Wonders if MAGA ‘Cult’ Is Over and More (Updating)

title: ‘Hinotama: Ball of Fire’ Review: Gentle, Handsomely Shot Domestic Drama Is a Promising Debut for Yaza Takenoshin
description: The early moments of “Hinotama: Ball of Fire,” the debut feature from young Japanese director Yaza Takenoshin (who graduated from Harvard this past
body:
The early moments of “Hinotama: Ball of Fire,” the debut feature from young Japanese director Yaza Takenoshin (who graduated from Harvard this past summer), almost move like clockwork, finding a pleasing rhythm in everyday mundanities — matching the repetition of numbers being called out for test papers to a mother having groceries counted at the checkout.

	Showing in the Nippon Cinema Now selection — a space for new and upcoming Japanese filmmakers — at the Tokyo Film Festival, the film follows young Takeshi (Riku Onishi) as he watches his parents’ marriage crumble. It’s a slow but clearly inevitable process, the warning signs understated but clear to see. Takeshi is getting worn down by glimpses of his parents’ flaws, and becomes fascinated with the “ball of fire” that his old friend Akari (Himena Irei) tells him about — perhaps in the hope that seeing it will restore his childlike wonder about the world.
	

	Yaza has spoken of his admiration for filmmakers such as Ryusuke Hamaguchi, which is evident in his film’s neat and steady (but never inert or emotionless) camerawork and its patient observation of characters as they navigate fracturing relationships. The inspiration is rather direct: “Himotama” is indeed shot by Hamaguchi’s sometime cinematographer Yoshio Kitagawa, who offered to shoot the film when the student reached out for advice. Often, Kitagawa’s cinematography embraces symmetry, emphasizing the clean geometric lines of Takeshi’s home, picking an object or person to place at the centre of the frame. A lot of these orderly compositions soon give off the impression of a cage — if Mari Kusu’s performance as Takeshi’s mother, bristling with frustration, didn’t already imply as much.
	

	Some terse dialogue soon cuts through that visual neatness, as Takeshi’s father hints at his dissatisfaction or frustration in a small aside — which then turns into a bigger fight, not long after as he “demands respect” and laments his children never thanking him. It all comes back to that earlier rhythm, a discontent from living as though on a factory line, where everything progresses with a subtle sense of automation and no feeling or passion. Takeshi drifts through all of these scenes without giving away his own dissatisfaction, until the dam bursts; destroying a pristine pair of sneakers by jumping in a muddy puddle, the moment all the more startling because of the stillness of the camera, and the length of Yaza’s takes to this point.

	Takeshi’s father is a petty and proud man, in ways continually expanded upon throughout the film’s runtime, though how he’s actually framed never truly changes. Rather, Yaza patiently accumulates small details about him. He isn’t plainly a terrible, angry person, at least not right away anyway: The beginning of a propagandist campaign to his children for the eventual split comes with the leveraging of memories clearly meaningful to them. Yaza seeks subdued performances from his actors in general, particularly in the case of Onishi as the increasingly insular but troubled Takeshi, whose frustrations with his parents mostly manifest in questions about that titular ball of fire, when he’s not gazing into space.

	Sometimes that muted approach can become a little overbearing — as in the shots of children standing in an orderly line as they watch Takeshi’s younger brother Kento (Koe Odani) walking to a new house. In moments, it feels a little unnatural, even compared to the deliberately uncomfortable family dynamic built in the film’s first third. A sudden jump forward to three months later destabilises the film to a greater extent, but there are still moments of pathos to be found, particularly as Kento is forced to grow up fast, taking initiative to try and alleviate the suffering of his family.

	“Hinotama” eventually ends up taking one step further into a more allegorical tone, which doesn’t fit with the film’s stronger elements — notably, its gradual observation of the increasingly visible cracks in a traditional family unit. Still, it’s an incredibly promising first feature.

schema.headline: ‘Hinotama: Ball of Fire’ Review: Gentle, Handsomely Shot Domestic Drama Is a Promising Debut for Yaza Takenoshin

title: Billy Evans Answers ‘You Can See Everything’ Burning Questions on Alleged Cocaine Use, Nathan Fielder Regrets and More
description: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ romantic partner and the villainous third wheel in Nathan Fielder’s “You Can See Everything,” has taken to social me
body:
Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ romantic partner and the villainous third wheel in Nathan Fielder’s “You Can See Everything,” has taken to social media to answer burning questions about the documentary.

	In a post on X Monday night, Evans invited viewers to “AMA” (ask me anything), with the addendum: “Needs to be legally permissable [sic].”

	Asked to pick one misconception about the film to dispel, Evans said, “That I somehow control Liz. Anyone who actually knows her would find that idea hilarious. She’s fiercely independent, strongwilled [sic], and my best friend. We are partners in every sense. We challenge each other, disagree, and face the world together. Her closest friends are also some of my closest friends. If I ever mistreated her, they’d have my head.”
	

	And asked if he regrets agreeing to the documentary, Evans wrote, “Not at all.” In case there was any doubt as to whether Evans was familiar with Fielder’s work, he said before the documentary he had seen “almost all of it.” Still, Evans said he and Holmes did “0” preparation ahead of filming with Fielder.

	Evans said they celebrated Fielder’s birthday during production, “around the table in Del Mar with my family.” He said Fielder missed the Time 100 dinner — the magazine named the comedian one of the 100 most influential people in 2023 — so they celebrated that too.

	Culture critic and podcast host Hunter Harris asked Evans whether he thought Christopher Abbott — who plays Evans in reenactments opposite Amanda Seyfried as Elizabeth Holmes — was miscast. Evasively, Evans replied, “Who is that?” 
	



	

									Courtesy Everett Collection
	



	One question that came up repeatedly was whether Evans was high on cocaine during the filming of the documentary, which had been speculated due to his frequent sniffing. “Never been a fan,” Evans said when asked directly about the drug. “Solo parenting 2 toddlers you are sick approx 75% of days. Allergies in Austin TX are no joke,” he wrote. In another post, he asked, “Please someone from Austin back me up here.”

	When one X user asked about his “facial bloating and the going insane part,” Evans responded, ” I got fat. Raising 2 kids alone, best friend in prison, depression, building a business. I ate more than I should. I was fat. Less so now. I prioritized my kids over my health. I’ve learned that I can find the time to do small things for myself again. And that eating after 10pm isn’t one of them.”

	In “You Can See Everything,” Evans explains to Fielder that he has been posting on Holmes’ social media accounts while the Theranos founder is incarcerated. Evans said he does not need to get Holmes’ approval for the posts because, essentially, he knows what she would say. Plus, he holds power of attorney for Holmes. 

	“We talk about everything, including X. Nothing happened behind her back,” Evans wrote underneath a question about his control of her social media. “The POA was simply the legal mechanism that allowed me to act on her behalf while she’s incarcerated. It was not a substitute for her consent.”



	

									A24
	



	Evans also weighed in on a few pop culture topics. Replying to music critic Anthony Fantano’s question, “is to pimp a butterfly a 10/10?,” Evans wrote, “Kendrick [Lamar] is a generational talent.” Asked about his “favorite pop diva,” Evans wrote, “Chappell Roan has one of the best live sets I have ever seen. The crowd was amazing. I bought our engagement ring at a Taylor Swift reputation tour merch stand. Aretha Franklin has the best voice.”

	His four favorite films are “The Fall,” “Alien,” “The Great Dictator” and “Primer.” And when asked about popular podcaster Ethan Klein being accused of cheating on his wife, Hila Klein, Evans said, “The moral superiority of EK is absurd. His wife had every right to shame him publicly.”

	On a sincere note, Evans replied to a few questions about Holmes. He said the first thing he will do when she gets out of prison is “hold our kids tight and talk all night.” And he wrote, “I miss everything about her. I miss her presence. Her touch. The way she runs her fingers through my hair. Her patience. She makes me a better person. And without her, I feel an emptiness that’s hard to describe. People often say they need someone when what they really mean is that they want them. I’ve thought a lot about that distinction. I need Liz. She should qualify as a medically necessary prescription.”
	

	What does he not miss about his partner? “Def not this,” he replied to someone suggesting “her scrambled eggs.”

title: ‘Just Before Dawn’ Producer Prevails in Cult Horror Courtroom Drama
description: A surreal legal battle unfolded last month in a courtroom in West Palm Beach, Fla., where a retired accountant faced off against a distributor of c
body:
A surreal legal battle unfolded last month in a courtroom in West Palm Beach, Fla., where a retired accountant faced off against a distributor of cult horror DVDs over ownership of a 1981 slasher film.

	The distributor, David DeFalco, goes by “The Demon” and taunted the accountant in a series of unhinged livestream videos, calling him and his lawyers “fucking maggots.”

	“We’ve got to defeat these scummy bastards,” DeFalco told his fans. “They’ve put huge damage to physical media.”
	

	That the case went to trial at all is unusual, and a testament to both sides’ commitment to principle regardless of legal costs. For the accountant, Vlado Hreljanovic, it was about reclaiming title to a movie he had made with his father, a Yugoslav producer who helped bring Milos Forman to the U.S. 

	Hreljanovic was young man when he put together financing for “Just Before Dawn,” a low-budget horror film set in the Oregon wilderness and starring George Kennedy. The film, which has grown in esteem over the years, was called “one of the most underrated slasher flicks of all time” by Horrornews.net and appeared on Variety‘s list of The 15 Scariest Films You’ve Never Seen.

	The rights have remained in the family, so Hreljanovic was startled to find, a few years ago, that the film was streaming on Shudder, the horror site, and that DVDs were selling on Amazon.

	“I never sold any of this to any of them,” he says.

	That discovery led to four years of litigation that culminated on Oct. 20, when a six-person jury found that DeFalco had infringed on Hreljanovic’s copyright. 
	

	DeFalco is a former wrestler and director of “Chaos,” a 2005 film that he calls “the most violent film ever made” (and which Roger Ebert called “ugly, nihilistic and cruel — a film I regret having seen.”) For DeFalco, the fight was about protecting the beleaguered cult DVD ecosystem from nefarious “copyright trolls.”

	Hreljanovic, now 79, spent most of his career in other businesses and is now retired. In 2012, he was approached by Bill “Banana Man” Olsen, who ran Code Red DVD and wanted to license “Just Before Dawn.” Hreljanovic agreed to a six-year deal, but was unhappy with having to chase him down for statements and decided to let it lapse in 2018.

	DeFalco was a partner of Olsen’s, and had launched his own horror DVD business, Dark Force Entertainment. By 2022 — four years after the contract had expired — Olsen was ailing and DeFalco was trying to scrape together money to pay for Olsen’s caregiver.

	“He gives me the title,” DeFalco says. “He says go license it to Shudder for two years.”

	Olsen had hundreds of such titles.

	“These things don’t do huge numbers,” DeFalco tells Variety, saying the “Just Before Dawn” deal reaped $10,000. “You have to put out tons of them. Do you think any of these old B-movies have a huge value in the marketplace?”

	Olsen died before the suit was filed, so Hreljanovic went after his estate and after his brother, Walt, who ran Scorpion Releasing. He also named AMC Networks, which owns Shudder, as well as Kino Lorber, Amazon, Target, Best Buy and Walmart. Walt Olsen died a few months later, and the other defendants reached out-of-court settlements — all except DeFalco.

	DeFalco took it personally that Hreljanovic would come after him and after the Olsens, his mentors in the DVD business.

	“I’m willing to destroy myself to get at you guys,” he said on a livestream. “This is going to be the war of the century.”

	DeFalco hyped up the dispute for his online fanbase. Wearing a white tank top and long black braids, he unleashed expletive-filled rants against Hreljanovic and his lawyers, calling them “fucking maggots.”

	“Why would you mess with the Demon?” DeFalco asked in one video, brandishing a blade. “I carve you to pieces with this!”
	

	Behind him, a man in a skull mask could be seen racking a shotgun. “This dude is a killer,” DeFalco said. “You want to fuck with us?! You really think that’s a good idea?”

	DeFalco’s legal argument was that Hreljanovic could not establish a chain of title to “Just Before Dawn.”

	“I don’t really know who the fuck owns it at this point, but I can tell you one person that don’t own it, and that’s fucking Vlado,” he said in a video. He also called the movie a “little shitbag, piece-of-garbage movie that his garbage-ass father made.”

	Hreljanovic had never met DeFalco and didn’t know quite what to make of it.

	“His language is very rosy,” Hreljanovic says. “He threatened me that he’s going to bankrupt me… He slandered my sister. I’ve never known this guy. I have no idea where he came from.”

	DeFalco ran up bills of about $200,000 on his legal defense. By the time of the trial, he was representing himself. He was not sure he would be able to do it, but he relied heavily on AI to draft his briefs — even winning a favorable pretrial ruling.

	He showed up to court with his braids, black shirt, and black shoes with flames on the side. It caught the eye of the courtroom staff and of the opposing side.

	“It was entertaining,” Hreljanovic said.

	At the trial, Hreljanovic’s lawyers sought to introduce the videos of DeFalco taunting their client — but the judge didn’t allow it.

	“I can’t even remember doing this,” DeFalco says. “I was going on and on. I was calling him every name in the book. They edit it in such a way to make it look like I was threatening them. I never threatened these guys.”

	Hreljanovic’s lawyers said that a key document — purportedly assigning the rights from Olsen to DeFalco — had been forged. And they also showed documents establishing that Hreljanovic still owns the copyright.

	“We proved the chain of title going back 45 years,” said Eric Lee, Hreljanovic’s lead trial attorney. “That was the most important issue to my client.”

	After two days of testimony and a day of deliberations, the jury found in Hreljanovic’s favor and awarded $46,000 — less than the maximum $150,000 — in statutory damages.

	DeFalco has no plans to pay, and is preparing to ask for a new trial. “There’s certain things the AI is putting together to file the motion,” he says, adding that he still plans to beat Hreljanovic “into submission.” But as he turns his attention to a new streaming venture, he is done with DVDs.
	

	“I’m getting rid of Dark Force,” he says, saying his “nice little lifestyle business” had been dealt a setback by the litigation. “I’ve had it with physical media.”

	Hreljanovic is happy that “Just Before Dawn” still has a cult following, and says he plans to bring out a 4K restoration next year. He says the trial was “an expensive exercise” and is relieved it’s over.

	“I’ll have more time to golf.”

            TikTok star Marcel Johnson is dead after battling stomach cancer ... and social media is gutted by the tragic loss.
      
    
            His wife, Taylor, announced on Instagram that he'd lost his cancer battle on Monday in a heartbreaking post.
      
    
            She wrote ... "November 2 2026 @ 445pm. I lost a whole entire half of me. He fought so hard for so long. He was so tired & exhausted & in so much pain."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Taylor continued ... "Yesterday the only words Marcel said all day were to me & Dedric and it was 'I'm ready to go' and that was in the morning. He still fought to hang on all day so we just got a bit more time."
      

            She says she's struggling to process the devastating loss ... "I truly don't even have words right now. I feel like this can't be real life. How can this be real f***ing life. I thought I was going to wake up and he was still going to be here beside me."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Taylor concluded ... "I love him with my whole entire being and life will absolutely never ever be the same."
      
    
            Marcel -- a father of 5 -- was diagnosed with cancer last August, and has spent the past 15 months documenting his battle on social media.
      
    
            He was 32.

            Chris Rock is diving into his faults as a husband ... namely, an overreliance on porn ... admitting he used to watch it all the time to the detriment of his marriage.
      
    
            The comedian discussed the taboo subject during his interview for GQ's Men of the Year issue ... pulling back the curtain on his marriage to Malaak Compton-Rock -- which ended back in 2016.
      
    
            Chris said, "I was not a great husband. I watched a lot of porn. I don't watch porn anymore. I haven't watched porn in five, six years.”
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Unclear if the porn fueled the bad behavior exactly ... though Chris seems to have those two facts linked in his mind for whatever reason.
      
    
            Chris said he's not proud about that time in his life ... but he added it's something he had to go through -- likening himself to a Marvel hero learning to be less selfish and embracing their truest self.
      
    
            He also opened up about his diagnosis with a nonverbal learning disorder ... saying it made him realize how insensitive much of his behavior through the years has been.
      
    
            Chris said, "Mental illness and celebrity ... it's a weird combination there, because you think people are reacting a certain way because of celebrity. Because it's this weird thing that you can't quantify. So I used to just blame everything on celebrity. It's like, 'Oh, we're not connecting because I had a chronic unique-ism.' I thought I was so f***ing unique."
      
    
            While Chris adds some of his trademark humor to the interview, it's a serious side of the comedian he doesn't usually show.

description:
Anonymous UK Celebrity
                          Spiraled After Sex Misconduct Claims
body:
Anonymous UK Celebrity
                          Spiraled After Sex Misconduct Claims
                          Publicist, Assistant Testify
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 3, 2026
                            10:19 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 3, 2026
                                12:30 PM PST
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The mystery UK celebrity accused of sexual misconduct spiraled after receiving letters from two major news outlets ... and his personal assistant later stepped in during a suicide attempt ... according to new documents from the case.
      
    
            TMZ obtained the filings detailing the anonymous star's battle to keep his identity hidden ... including testimony from his personal assistant, publicist and attorney.
      
    
            According to the docs ... the celebrity received letters from ITN and The Guardian in May asking him to respond to allegations of sexual misconduct.
      
    
            His personal assistant told the court the letters triggered an immediate and dramatic change in the celebrity's behavior ... saying he couldn't cope with the prospect of negative publicity and expressed a desire to take his own life.
      
    
            The docs say things got so serious that the celebrity was voluntarily admitted to a psychiatric hospital that same day ... with his publicist saying he initially couldn't respond to the allegations because of his mental state.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            But, according to the filing, the situation took another troubling turn in July ... when the celebrity left the hospital during a period of leave and attempted to take his own life. His personal assistant became aware of his movements and intervened, according to the docs.
      
    
            In a recorded October conversation with his lawyer, the celebrity also claimed he'd concealed or downplayed his suicidal intentions to get hospital restrictions eased and eventually secure his release.
      
    
            He also expressed fears that the allegations becoming public could destroy his relationship with his son ... a concern his legal team cited while fighting to keep his identity secret.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... the man, identified only as "PPT" in court, is accused of abusing his fame and influence to pursue inappropriate sexual relationships with much younger women. He has denied the allegations.
      
    
            Judge Matthew Nicklin ruled the celebrity couldn't stop the allegations from being published ... but his name will remain undisclosed for now while he has a chance to appeal.
      
    
            The judge did not rule whether the sexual misconduct allegations were true.
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.
